comparator.name: Global Sustainability Science
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 curriculum for the Fall 2026 cohort, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026-2027 programme-specific EER governs the 2026 entrant and defines a 135-EC major plus a 45-EC optional course profile. The major consists of 60 EC of compulsory courses and 75 EC of major choices. The generic target does not name one of the five tracks; none is formally broader or less specialised than the others, so the first-listed Water, Climate & Ecosystems track is selected by official order before considering UCR fit. Its required major choices are Chemistry and the Environment (7.5 EC), Global Climate Change (7.5), Ecological Field Research (7.5), Ecohydrology (7.5) and the 15-EC WCE thesis. The first-listed non-track choices instantiate Philosophy of Science and Ethics (7.5) and the ordinary Consultancy Project (7.5). The EER requires two further distinct advanced courses from a shared list; after excluding Ecohydrology because it is already the track core, the first two available listed choices are Landscape Ecology and Nature Conservation and Environmental Chemistry and Health (7.5 EC each). Together with the 60-EC compulsory core these choices total 135 EC. The remaining 45 EC is genuine optional-course-profile space for extra major courses, a minor, approved external study, study abroad or internship, and is preserved without invented content.

alternatives.label: Water, climate, ecosystems & sustainable food
alternatives.concept: An integrated sustainability-science programme centred on water, climate and ecosystems, with sustainable food, environmental justice and governance. Mathematical, statistical, spatial and field methods support evidence-based environmental research.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule follows the selected Water, Climate & Ecosystems route while adding a coherent sustainable-food and ecology strand.
progression: Sustainability, Earth-system, ecology, economics and methods foundations precede spatial analysis, hydrology, upper-level environmental science, statistics, governance and partner-facing research; prerequisites and term offerings pass.

alternatives.label: Sustainability governance & societal transformation
alternatives.concept: A sustainability route focused on institutions, law, policy, justice, political mobilisation and public communication, grounded in climate, environmental science, economics, data and applied sustainability research.
alternatives.labelReason: Governance, politics, law, environmental justice and climate communication form the scheduled focus while environmental science supplies the problem context.
progression: Sustainability, law, politics, economics, research and data foundations precede international law, public economics, advanced EU politics, governance, conflict analysis and applied sustainability research; prerequisites and term offerings pass.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces ecology, hazards, aquifers, sustainable farming and advanced quantitative depth with a sequenced law, politics, justice and communication curriculum.

alternatives.label: Sustainable business, energy & resources
alternatives.concept: Links sustainable business models and organisational innovation to renewable energy, resource geoscience, circular material flows, economics and governance. Data, research and environmental media place business decisions in their wider societal context.
alternatives.labelReason: Business, innovation and leadership are combined with a sequenced energy, resource and circular-economy curriculum.
progression: Business, sustainability, economics, methods and Earth-science foundations precede advanced public economics, energy design, resource research, leadership, econometrics and international business governance; prerequisites and term offerings pass.
alternatives.distinctness: This route substitutes entrepreneurship, circularity, renewable-system design, organisational innovation and international business for the closest route's ecology, hazards, water-management and advanced mathematics emphasis.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target has five equally formal tracks and none is clearly broader or less specialised than the others. The current official programme page and EER list Water, Climate & Ecosystems first, so it is selected by official order before considering UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Two additional generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible after the closest match: Governance & Societal Transformation and a combined Business & Innovation plus Energy & Resources route. Both are substantively distinct and exceed the 30-EC pairwise course-difference floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

blocks: Sustainability systems, climate, water and ecology
Both address ecology, biodiversity and conservation; the comparator course is advanced and landscape-focused.
Both examine water movement through soils and aquifers; the comparator course has a broader ecosystem-water focus.
Both connect societal choices to sustainability interventions; the UCR course is nature-based engineering rather than a social-science foundation.
Both address multi-actor sustainability transformations; the comparator component is a larger integrated project.
Both examine environmental chemistry and material contamination; UCR focuses on recovery and remediation.
Both examine chemical processes and contaminants in environmental systems; the comparator also emphasizes human health.
Methods, projects, research and open space
Both provide quantitative data analysis; the comparator course is programme-specific statistics.
Both are interdisciplinary, field-informed sustainability projects; the comparator project is specifically regional and based on Texel.
The required ecological field-research course has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
The selected philosophy-of-science and ethics course has no single course in these UCR schedules.
The compulsory 15-EC individual thesis cannot be counted as an ordinary UCR course or UCR's optional research element.
The dedicated external consultancy project is not identical to an ordinary UCR course.
The genuine 45-EC optional course profile remains student-selected and is not a fixed external course to align.

notes.text: Utrecht's BSc combines a 60-EC interdisciplinary core with a formal 75-EC track and a 45-EC optional profile. UCR can build three coherent sustainability programmes, but it does not reproduce the selected track's required ecological field course, dedicated consultancy project or compulsory 15-EC thesis; pairings indicate intellectual overlap rather than transfer equivalence.
